notes: Source: the web edition of Water Safety New Zealand's 2025 Drowning Prevention Report (released 19 Feb 2026, data correct as of 19 Feb 2026), 'Detailed breakdown', which has six activity sections in this order: Swimming, Craft, Fishing from land, Underwater, Slips and falls, Other recreation. Four print a 2025 count in their text: Swimming 15 (14 of the 15 male), Craft 17 (seven of them on craft in tidal environments), Fishing from land 10 (all male) and Slips and falls 24. Each is entered as printed, one row per section, grade A. Underwater and Other recreation print no count in their text; their counts sit in Infogram charts that render client-side and in the Dropbox PDF, which was not attempted. Those two are entered as gap rows (grade D, null low and high), as the ledger already does for the Pools and Home settings; the reviewer may prefer to drop them. Status partial for that reason. 2024 comparisons: the 2025 web edition prints one, for fishing from land only ('three more than the previous year', under 'Key statistics'), which makes 2024 seven as the report counts it (an implication, recorded as such, not a printed 2024 count). No 2024 figure, year-on-year change or activity-specific 10-year average is printed for swimming, craft, underwater, slips and falls or other recreation. The media release adds a 10-year average of six for land-based fishing. The 2024 report web page prints shares, not counts (Slips and falls 28%, Craft 25%, Swimming/'playing in the water' 25% of 72 deaths); these are noted but not converted to counts, since 72 has since been revised (the 2025 report treats 2024 as 74). Nothing was summed. The four printed counts do not reach 78 and must not be summed to it: the web edition shows no non-recreational, unknown or 'other' activity section, so the six sections may not partition the total; whether 'Craft' includes commercial or non-recreational boating, and whether 'Underwater' covers snorkelling and free-diving as well as scuba, is not defined on the web edition. Activity and setting are two different partitions of the same 78: Craft (17) equals Rivers (17) by coincidence; swimming is the highest-risk activity in inland still water and slips and falls the leading cause in rivers, per the setting sections already in the ledger. The counts are on the 78 basis (Feb 2026 printing); WSNZ's Drowning Insights page gives the provisional 2025 total as 79 by Oct 2026 and no revised activity split was found. One correction is proposed, to the note of new-zealand-total-2025, pointing to the activity rows, and only if they are merged. No names, contact details or precise positions were recorded. Infogram chart ids for each activity section are given in the evidence so a browser-equipped follow-up can read the two missing counts.
